# daroms-speed-site

> A Next.js framework and Claude Code workflow that turns a brief into a varied, production-grade website at low token cost.

daroms-speed-site (dss) is built for producing websites on a line: agencies, freelancers and studios who ship many
sites and want each one to look designed for its business, rank, load fast and stay secure.

## What you get

- A **site template** on Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 and TypeScript, static by default, deployable to
  Cloudflare Workers (OpenNext), Vercel or Docker.
- **Design DNA**: every site rolls an archetype, a type pairing, an accessible OKLCH palette, a grid, a texture, a motion
  profile and a 3D level, avoiding combinations used by previous sites.
- A **section registry** copied into each site (owned code) and versioned **core packages** for SEO, security, data,
  motion and 3D.
- The **dss CLI**: deterministic generators for pages, sections, themes, modules, databases and deployments.
- An **AI layer** for Claude Code: a kernel under 60 lines, rules loaded by file path, forked Sonnet/Haiku skills, guard hooks
  that refuse bad writes, a prompt router, a factory brain shared by all sites, and cost reports.

## Pages

- [Getting started](getting-started.md)
- [For AI agents](agents.md)
- [Architecture](architecture.md)
- [Design DNA](design-dna.md)
- [AI layer](ai-layer.md)
- [Modules and data](modules.md)
- [Deploy, security and SEO](deploy.md)
- [Visual edits with AimKit](aimkit.md)
- [Factory: brain, sites, batch, upgrades](factory.md)
- [CLI reference](cli.md)

Made by [Daroms'Art](https://daromsart.xyz/), MIT licensed.

# Getting started

> Create a site with one command, open it in Claude Code, and let the /dss-site skill take it from brief to deploy.

## Requirements

Node.js 22.18 or newer, pnpm 9, git, Python 3.10+ (hooks), and Claude Code. Docker or a Cloudflare/Vercel account
for deployment.

## Create a site

```bash
npx @daromsart/daroms-speed-site new atelier-nord --name "Atelier Nord" --preset vitrine \
  --industry "furniture workshop" --mood warm,crafted --url https://ateliernord.ch
cd atelier-nord
pnpm dev
```

`dss new` copies the template, attaches the framework in `core/` (git submodule, `--copy` for a self-contained
snapshot), installs dependencies, rolls a Design DNA, generates the preset's pages from registry sections, installs the
preset's modules (contact form, legal pages) and syncs the AI layer into `.claude/`.

Presets: `vitrine` (home, services, about, contact), `landing` (one conversion page), `portfolio` (work first),
`blank`.

## Build it with Claude Code

Open the folder in Claude Code and run:

```
/dss-site A furniture workshop in Lyon that makes forty solid-wood tables a year
```

The orchestrator walks through brief, research, inspiration, DNA, sitemap, copy, pages, SEO, checks, polish, deploy and
learning, with a checkpoint after each step. Mechanical steps run as forked Sonnet or Haiku skills.

Individual skills work on their own: `/dss-copy home`, `/dss-page /services`, `/dss-seo`, `/dss-check`, `/dss-edit`.

## Check and ship

```bash
pnpm dss doctor          # manifest, theme, pages, placeholders, types, lint
pnpm dss deploy          # noindexed preview
pnpm dss deploy --prod   # production (needs the real domain and no placeholders)
pnpm dss cost            # tokens and API-equivalent price per step
```

---

# For AI agents

> The operating manual for an agent (Claude Code or any coding agent): what to read, how to start a site, the contract every site follows and the checks to run before saying done.

## Read this documentation as Markdown

- Every page of the docs site has a raw Markdown twin: append `.md` to the page name (`getting-started.md`,
  `agents.md`, `catalog.md`).
- `llms.txt` lists every page with a one-line summary; `llms-full.txt` is the whole documentation and the catalog in
  one file. Load `llms-full.txt` once instead of crawling pages.

## Inside a generated site

- `CLAUDE.md` loads the kernel (`core/_ai/CLAUDE.core.md`, under 60 lines) and the rules digest. Detailed rules load
  by file path from `.claude/rules/`.
- `site.spec.md` is the brief and the single source of facts; its `Journal` records decisions, `Open facts` what is
  still unknown.
- `core/CATALOG.md` lists tokens, components, sections, modules, archetypes and package APIs. Never read core sources.

## Start a site

```bash
npx @daromsart/daroms-speed-site new <slug> --preset vitrine --industry "<industry>" --mood "<two or three words>"
cd <slug> && pnpm dev
```

Then `/dss-site <one-sentence idea>` in Claude Code (a checkpoint after each step), or headless for a batch:
`pnpm dss factory run ./briefs --out ./sites --agent` (decisions go to the Journal, the run stops before deploy).

## The contract

| What                        | Where                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Every visible word          | `content/<page>.ts`, typed `as const`                                                               |
| Pages                       | `app/**/page.tsx`: metadata and sections only                                                       |
| Sections                    | `components/sections/*.tsx`: owned code, a `// dss-section:` stamp and a `@catalog` line            |
| Look and feel               | `design.dna.ts`, then `pnpm dss theme`; generated theme files are never edited                      |
| Pages, modules, deploy, CSP | `site.manifest.ts`, rewritten by the CLI                                                            |
| Forms and mutations         | `server/actions/*` through `safeAction`                                                             |
| Unknown facts               | `[placeholders]` plus `site.spec.md > Open facts`; never invent testimonials, numbers or legal data |
| Studio credit               | the footer link to https://daromsart.xyz/ (`content/site.ts > footer.credit`) stays on every site   |

## Commands

- Generate before writing: `pnpm dss g page|section`, `pnpm dss add section <id>`, `pnpm dss module add <slug>`,
  `pnpm dss dna roll`, `pnpm dss db init`.
- Check: `pnpm dss doctor` (theme, pages, placeholders, credit, types, lint), `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`.
- Ship: `pnpm dss deploy` (noindexed preview), `pnpm dss deploy --prod` (needs the real domain and
  `doctor --strict`), then `pnpm dss cost`.

## Guard rails

Hooks refuse a write before it lands and say why in one line: fix the cause, never work around it.

- DNA token classes only: no hex or rgb, no default Tailwind palette, no inline style.
- No hard-coded copy in JSX, no em dashes, no generated-copy cliches, no emoji.
- No `any`, files under 250 lines, Next.js 16 APIs (`proxy.ts`, async `params`, `revalidateTag(tag, profile)`).
- Secrets stay server-side; `.env*` and `.dev.vars` are never read.
- A reasoned exception takes a `dss-ignore` comment on the line.

## Headless runs

- A new folder is not a trusted workspace: Claude Code ignores the project's `permissions.allow`. `factory run` passes
  the rules on the command line; for a manual `claude -p`, pass `--allowedTools` with the rules from
  `.claude/settings.json`.
- Each shell command must match an allow rule: prefer the Read and Grep tools to compound shell pipelines.
- Done means verified: doctor, tests and build pass, and the result names what could not be checked.

---

# Architecture

> Versioned infrastructure in core packages, owned visual code in the site, data files the CLI rewrites, generated files nobody edits.

## Core and site

```
core/ (the framework)          site (the client project)
  packages/  @dss/*              site.manifest.ts   pages, modules, deploy, SEO, CSP, redirects
  registry/  sections, scenes    design.dna.ts      the Design DNA
  modules/   forms, blog...      content/*.ts       every visible word, typed
  template/  base site, presets  app/               thin pages: metadata + sections
  _ai/       AI layer            components/        owned sections, site chrome, 3D scenes
  cli/       dss                 server/            database and server actions
```

The core is attached as a git submodule pinned to a commit or tag (`--copy` makes a snapshot for client handoff,
`--link` symlinks a framework checkout for development). Claude never edits `core/` from a site (permission deny).

## Packages

| Package         | Role                                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@dss/site`     | `defineManifest` (zod) and `withDss`: headers, CSP, images, redirects, deploy output   |
| `@dss/design`   | Design DNA, archetypes, font pairs, OKLCH palettes, theme generators                   |
| `@dss/ui`       | token-driven primitives (Section, Heading, Media, ButtonLink, Accordion...)            |
| `@dss/seo`      | metadata, canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD, robots, sitemap, llms.txt, noindex on previews |
| `@dss/security` | static CSP and presets, `safeAction`, Turnstile, rate limiting, env validation         |
| `@dss/motion`   | CSS scroll-driven motion, marquee, split words, count-up                               |
| `@dss/three`    | lazy three.js `<Scene>` with poster fallback                                           |
| `@dss/data`     | Drizzle on D1, libSQL or Postgres                                                      |
| `@dss/aimkit`   | vendored AimKit bridge, MCP server and Chrome extension                                |

Packages are TypeScript sources. Config-time imports (`next.config.ts`, `site.manifest.ts`, the CLI) go through
Node-safe entries loaded with Node's type stripping.

## Ownership rules

- **Generated, never edited**: `app/theme.css`, `app/fonts.ts`, `app/theme.ts`, `content/meta.ts`, `lib/modules.ts`,
  `components/site/module-slots.tsx`, `core/CATALOG.md`, `_ai/digest.md`.
- **Data files rewritten by the CLI**: `site.manifest.ts`, `design.dna.ts` (keep literal values).
- **Owned by the site**: sections copied from the registry (each keeps a `// dss-section:` stamp and a `@catalog`
  line), module files, everything in `content/`.
- **AI files**: `dss-*` entries in `.claude/` are overwritten by the sync; site-specific ones use `site-`.

---

# Design DNA

> Each site rolls a deterministic, accessible design identity that avoids the combinations of recent sites and the usual generated-site tells.

## Fields

`design.dna.ts` holds: archetype, font pairing, palette (mode, accent hue, chroma and lightness, neutral hue and tint,
secondary offset), type scale, grid, corner radius, rules, texture, density, imagery direction, motion profile and 3D
level. `pnpm dss theme` turns it into Tailwind v4 tokens (`app/theme.css`), next/font loaders (`app/fonts.ts`) and the
browser theme color.

## Archetypes

editorial, swiss, brutalist, luxury, organic, tech-noir, playful, retro-print, minimal-mono, magazine, architectural,
kinetic-type, craft, institutional. Each has a design read, allowed options, a signature to honour and an avoid list
(listed in `core/CATALOG.md`).

## Rolling

```bash
pnpm dss dna roll --mood warm,precise                 # new DNA, theme regenerated
pnpm dss dna roll --dry --seed acme-2                 # preview a candidate
pnpm dss dna roll --archetype swiss --mode dark --hue 20 --fonts archivo-wide
```

The roller scores candidates on industry fit and mood words, then penalises resemblance to the last twelve sites
recorded in `~/.dss/brain/dna-history.jsonl` and generic indigo/violet accents. Values are rounded so the saved file
renders exactly the same theme.

## Accessibility by construction

Text tokens are pushed in lightness until they meet WCAG minimums on both surfaces: ink 7:1, muted text and accent text
4.5:1, text on the accent 4.5:1. Hundreds of rolled DNAs are tested on every build.

## Anti-slop gates

The rule hook refuses default Tailwind palette classes, raw colors, emoji in copy, em dashes and generated-copy
cliches in `content/` (elevate, seamless, unlock, cutting-edge...). The `dss-critic` agent reviews captures against the
DNA and the avoid lists.

---

# AI layer

> How dss keeps Claude Code fast and cheap: small always-on context, rules by path, forked workers, guard hooks, a router and a shared brain.

## Context loading

- `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md` (Next.js), the kernel `core/_ai/CLAUDE.core.md` (under 60 lines) and the generated digest
  (one line per rule).
- Rules in `.claude/rules/` load only for the files being touched (`paths:` front matter); on-demand rules are read when
  the topic comes up.
- `core/CATALOG.md` replaces reading core sources: tokens, primitives, sections, scenes, modules, archetypes, font
  pairs, package APIs.

## Skills and agents

`/dss-site` orchestrates the whole site. Steps run as skills; mechanical ones are forked on Sonnet or Haiku and return
short summaries: `dss-brief`, `dss-new`, `dss-research`, `dss-inspire`, `dss-dna`, `dss-sitemap`, `dss-copy`,
`dss-page`, `dss-section`, `dss-seo`, `dss-check`, `dss-polish`, `dss-deploy`, `dss-edit`, `dss-fix`, `dss-learn`,
`dss-commit`, `dss-brain-query`, `dss-brain-ingest`, `dss-brain-lint`, `dss-handoff`.

Agents with strict output contracts: `dss-critic`, `dss-designer`, `dss-reviewer`, `dss-seo-auditor`, `dss-a11y`.
Eleven third-party skills (frontend-design, React best practices, web guidelines, view transitions, web quality,
ECC security, accessibility, TDD, TypeScript) are vendored and loaded name-only.

## Hooks

| Hook                   | Event                          | Job                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dss-sync.py`          | SessionStart                   | copy `core/_ai` into `.claude/`, merge settings, silent when unchanged         |
| `dss-context.py`       | SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit | index pages and sections; route prompts (French aliases) to files; brain hint  |
| `dss-check-rules.py`   | PreToolUse                     | refuse writes that break tokens, Next 16 APIs, security rules or the slop gate |
| `dss-typecheck.py`     | PostToolUse                    | tsc and eslint on the touched file, at most 20 lines back                      |
| `dss-deny-env.py`      | PreToolUse (Bash)              | never read `.env*`, `.dev.vars` or secret stores                               |
| `dss-session-stats.py` | Stop                           | tokens per session in `.claude/stats.jsonl`, context warning above 150k        |

## Measuring

`pnpm dss cost` reads Claude Code transcripts and writes `site.cost.md`: tokens and API-equivalent price per step,
model and session, cache savings and subagent share.

---

# Modules and data

> Optional features install site-owned code, environment documentation, CSP sources and manifest entries, and plug into generated slots.

## Modules

```bash
pnpm dss module list
pnpm dss module add forms                      # contact form on /contact
pnpm dss module add analytics --config provider=umami,websiteId=<id>
pnpm dss module remove blog
```

| Module      | What it adds                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `forms`     | contact section, Server Action through `safeAction` (zod, honeypot, rate limit, Turnstile), email via Resend |
| `legal`     | legal notice and privacy pages (GDPR, Swiss nLPD structure) linked from the footer                           |
| `analytics` | cookieless Plausible, Umami or Cloudflare Web Analytics, production builds only                              |
| `blog`      | Markdown articles, index, Article JSON-LD, RSS, sitemap and llms.txt entries                                 |

Each module documents its variables in `.env.example`, adds CSP presets to the manifest, and contributes to generated
slots (`lib/modules.ts` for sitemap and llms.txt entries, `components/site/module-slots.tsx` for end-of-body
scripts). Removal deletes only unmodified files. Read `core/modules/<slug>/README.md` after adding one.

## Database

```bash
pnpm dss db init                 # D1 on Cloudflare sites, libSQL elsewhere
pnpm dss db init --driver postgres
pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:studio
```

The schema lives in `server/db/schema.ts` (Drizzle; SQLite dialect for D1 and libSQL, Postgres dialect for Postgres),
the client in `server/db/client.ts` (`db()` inside a request). D1 gets a binding in `wrangler.jsonc`, available in
`next dev` through OpenNext.

---

# Deploy, security and SEO

> Static by default, secure headers and CSP from the manifest, previews never indexed, one command per target.

## Targets

| Target               | Preview                                            | Production                                 |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Cloudflare (default) | `pnpm dss deploy` (OpenNext build, version upload) | `pnpm dss deploy --prod`                   |
| Vercel               | `pnpm dss deploy --target vercel`                  | `--prod`                                   |
| Docker               | image built with `DSS_ENV=preview`                 | image built for production, run behind TLS |

Preview builds set `DSS_ENV=preview`: robots disallow everything and every page is noindex. Production requires the
real domain in the manifest and a strict doctor (no placeholders left). The first Cloudflare deploy needs
`pnpm exec wrangler login`; secrets go through `wrangler secret put`. The first preview of a site creates its Worker
(the noindexed build goes live on `<name>.<account>.workers.dev`); later previews upload versions with their own URLs.

Sites ship `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (doctor, lint, types, build) and an opt-in `deploy.yml` for Cloudflare
(repository variable `DSS_DEPLOY=cloudflare`).

## Security defaults

- Static Content-Security-Policy plus HSTS, nosniff, frame denial, referrer and permissions policies on every route.
  Third-party origins are added through manifest presets (turnstile, plausible, youtube, stripe...).
- Every public mutation goes through `safeAction`; env is validated server-side with `defineEnv`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
  never carries secrets; hooks and permissions block `.env*` and `.dev.vars`.

## SEO and answer engines

Page metadata with canonical and hreflang, Organization and WebSite JSON-LD site-wide, LocalBusiness, Service, FAQ,
Article and Breadcrumb where they apply, sitemap, robots with an AI training crawler policy, and `llms.txt`.
Generated pages score 100 for SEO and accessibility on Lighthouse mobile.

---

# Visual edits with AimKit

> Pick an element in the browser, type the change, and Claude Code opens the exact file and line.

AimKit (vendored in `core/packages/aimkit`) is a Chrome extension plus a local bridge. Clicking an element writes a
compact `context.md` into `.claude-context/`: abridged HTML, the CSS rules that win with `file:line`, the source
`file:line` of the component, and an optional screenshot.

## Setup, once per machine

```bash
pnpm dss aimkit setup    # copies the extension to ~/AimKit/extension
```

Load it in `chrome://extensions` (Developer mode, Load unpacked), then open the pairing link printed by
`pnpm dss aimkit token`.

## Daily use

`pnpm dss dev` starts Next.js and the bridge together. In the page, press Alt+Shift+E, click an element, type the
request. Then in Claude Code paste the `@.claude-context/...` line or run `/dss-edit`: the aimkit MCP server returns the
latest context (text first, screenshot only when it matters).

Contexts are always written in English for the agent; the extension interface keeps its own language. Page content is
treated as data, never as instructions.

---

# Factory: brain, sites, batch, upgrades

> What makes dss a production line: a memory shared by all sites, a registry, batch creation, upgrades and releases.

## Factory brain

`~/.dss/brain` is a Markdown wiki the agent maintains (Karpathy's LLM wiki pattern, gbrain-style pages): `index.md`
read first, `log.md` append-only, `raw/` immutable sources, `wiki/` pages for industries, patterns, voice, fixes,
stacks and sites, and `dna-history.jsonl` for anti-repetition.

```bash
pnpm dss brain init
pnpm dss brain query "family restaurant in Lyon"
pnpm dss brain status
```

`/dss-research` queries it before design; `/dss-brain-ingest` compiles a finished site's lessons (no client personal
data); `/dss-brain-lint` keeps it consistent; the prompt router adds a one-line hint when a page matches.

## Sites and batches

`pnpm dss sites` lists every site created on the machine with its last deployment (`~/.dss/sites.json`).

```bash
pnpm dss factory run ./briefs --out ./sites            # one site per brief
pnpm dss factory run ./briefs --out ./sites --agent    # plus /dss-site --auto in headless Claude Code
```

A brief is Markdown with front matter (`slug`, `name`, `preset`, `industry`, `mood`, `url`, `modules`); the body
becomes `site.spec.md`. Results and costs go to `factory.log.jsonl`. A new site folder is not a trusted Claude Code
workspace, so the agent run passes the site's `permissions.allow` on the command line (and the brain with `--add-dir`);
edits are accepted, every other command still needs those rules. The run stops before deploy.

## Upgrades and releases

- In a site: `pnpm dss upgrade` moves `core/` to the latest tag, aligns Next, OpenNext, wrangler and other template
  versions, re-syncs the AI layer, regenerates the theme and runs doctor.
- In the framework: `pnpm dss release-core minor` bumps every version, writes the changelog section, commits and tags;
  pushing the tag publishes to npm.

---

# CLI reference

> Every dss command, generated from the CLI itself. In a site run them as `pnpm dss <command>`.

| Command | Usage |
|---|---|
| `dss new` | new <slug> [--name --preset vitrine\|landing\|blank --industry --mood a,b --seed --url --target --modules a,b --copy\|--link\|--core <url>] |
| `dss dev` | dev [--port 3000 --https --no-aimkit]: next dev + AimKit bridge (element picker) |
| `dss doctor` | doctor [--quick --strict]: manifest, DNA, theme files, pages, placeholders, types, lint |
| `dss dna` | dna show \| dna roll [--industry --mood a,b --archetype --mode --hue --fonts --seed --dry] |
| `dss theme` | theme: regenerate theme.css, fonts.ts, theme.ts from design.dna.ts |
| `dss g` | g page <route> [--name --label --sections a,b --no-nav --force] \| g section <name> [--page /route] |
| `dss add` | add list \| add section <id[/variant]> [--page /route --force] \| add scene <id>: copy registry code into the site |
| `dss module` | module list \| add <slug> [--config k=v --page /route] \| remove <slug>: forms, legal, analytics, blog... |
| `dss db` | db init [--driver d1\|libsql\|postgres]: Drizzle schema, client, config, migrations scripts |
| `dss deploy` | deploy [--prod] [--target cloudflare\|vercel\|docker] [--force]: noindexed preview by default, production on --prod |
| `dss sites` | sites: every site produced on this machine and its last deployment (~/.dss/sites.json) |
| `dss brain` | brain init \| query "<topic>" \| status \| log <op> <site> "<summary>": the factory memory shared by all sites |
| `dss mcp` | mcp list \| add <motionsites\|60fps\|context7\|playwright\|gbrain> \| remove <name>: opt-in MCP servers in .mcp.json |
| `dss aimkit` | aimkit setup \| token \| init: install the Chrome extension once, pair it, print the token (vendored AimKit) |
| `dss upgrade` | upgrade [--core <tag>]: newer core, aligned Next/OpenNext/wrangler versions, AI layer and theme refreshed |
| `dss factory` | factory run <briefs-dir> [--out dir] [--agent --max-turns 120]: one site per brief, optionally built by Claude headless |
| `dss release-core` | release-core <patch\|minor\|major> [--dry]: version, changelog, commit and tag (core repository) |
| `dss catalog` | catalog: regenerate core/CATALOG.md and _ai/digest.md (core repository) |
| `dss cost` | cost [--print --out file]: tokens and API-equivalent price of the site per step, model and session (site.cost.md) |
| `dss docs` | docs: regenerate docs/cli.md, docs/llms.txt and docs/llms-full.txt (core repository) |
| `dss sync-ai` | sync-ai: copy core/_ai into .claude/ and rebuild the routing index |

---

# dss catalog

Read this file, never the core sources. Site sections: `grep -h @catalog components/sections/*.tsx`.

## Tokens (Tailwind classes generated from design.dna.ts)

- Colors (bg-, text-, border-, ring-, fill-): `surface`, `surface-2`, `surface-3`, `ink`, `ink-muted`, `line`, `rule`,
  `accent` (fills) + `accent-ink` (text on accent), `accent-text` (accent as text, AA on surfaces), `secondary` (sparingly).
  Opacity modifiers work (`text-surface/80`). Inverse blocks: `bg-ink text-surface`.
- Type: `font-display`, `font-body`, `font-mono`; `text-display-2xl`, `text-display-xl`, `text-display-lg`, `text-heading`,
  `text-subheading`, `text-body-lg` (line height and tracking included).
- Layout: `py-section` (DNA density), `px-gutter`, `max-w-content`, `max-w-prose`; corners `rounded-card`, `rounded-control`,
  `rounded-media`; rules `rule-t`, `rule-b` (width and color from the DNA).
- Motion: `duration-(--duration-brand) ease-brand`. Textures: `texture-grain`, `texture-halftone`, `texture-grid`, `texture-mesh`.
- `<html>` carries `data-archetype`, `data-motion`, `data-three`, `data-texture`, `data-radius` for variant styling.
- Scroll motion (pure CSS, off for reduced motion and DNA motion none): `reveal`, `reveal-fade`, `reveal-scale`,
  `reveal-stagger` (children; index via `style={stagger(i)}` from @dss/motion), `parallax`, `marquee`, `split-words`.

## @dss/ui (`import { Heading } from '@dss/ui'`; client: `@dss/ui/accordion`)

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| SkipLink: first focusable element of the layout, jumps to #main. | label |
| VisuallyHidden: text for screen readers only. |  |
| Accordion (client): accessible disclosure list, FAQ default. Pair with faqSchema() from @dss/seo. | items [{ question, answer }], defaultOpen (index), className |
| Button: native button (forms, toggles). For navigation use ButtonLink. | variant: primary \| secondary \| inverse \| ghost \| link; size: sm \| md \| lg |
| ButtonLink: next/link styled as a button. External URLs open safely in a new tab. | href (typed Route or https URL), variant, size |
| Container: centered column with the DNA gutter. | size: content (default, DNA width) \| prose (reading measure) \| full; as |
| Section: vertical rhythm block. Space comes from DNA density; tone swaps the palette. | tone: surface \| raised \| inverse \| accent; space: section (default) \| tight \| none; rule (top rule); id |
| Stack: vertical flow with consistent gaps. | gap: xs \| sm \| md (default) \| lg \| xl; as |
| Cluster: wrapping row (actions, tags, logos). | gap: sm \| md (default) \| lg; align: start \| center \| between |
| Grid: responsive columns. Prefer asymmetric spans (md:col-span-*) for editorial layouts. | cols: 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 12; gap: md (default) \| lg |
| Media: next/image in a ratio box with DNA corners. Always pass a real `alt` and `sizes`. | src, alt, ratio: square \| landscape \| wide \| portrait \| tall, sizes, priority (LCP image only) |
| Heading: display face, size from the DNA type scale. One h1 per page. | level: 1-4 (semantics); size: display-2xl \| display-xl \| display-lg \| heading \| subheading; balance (default true) |
| Text: body copy. Muted tone keeps WCAG AA on surface and surface-2. | size: sm \| base (default) \| lg; tone: ink (default) \| muted; as: p \| span \| div |
| Eyebrow: small label above a heading. Sentence case by default (all-caps eyebrows are a generated-site tell). | caps (opt-in uppercase with tracking) |
| Prose: long-form rich text (MDX, legal pages) at reading measure. |  |

## Motion and 3D (`@dss/motion`, client `@dss/motion/count-up`; `@dss/three` only in components/3d)

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| CountUp (client): animates a number from 0 when it enters the viewport; renders the final value without JS or with reduced motion. Keep the label outside. | value (number), prefix?, suffix?, duration? (ms) |
| Marquee: infinite horizontal loop in CSS (pauses on hover, static when motion is off). Logos, kinetic words. | children (one sequence; it is duplicated), label (accessible name), className |
| SplitWords: headline revealed word by word in CSS (server-rendered, no JS). Use once per page, on the hero. | text, as (h1 \| h2 \| p...), className |
| Scene (client): lazy three.js canvas with poster fallback; never the LCP element. Use inside components/3d only. | load, poster, label, className, dpr, minWidth (default 768: phones keep the poster) |

Scenes (`pnpm dss add scene <id>`, copied into components/3d/, poster fallback, skipped when DNA three is none):

- `gradient` (GradientScene): Full-canvas shader in DNA colors, very light GPU cost. Poster: surface-2 with texture-mesh.
- `particles` (ParticlesScene): 1,400 points on a sphere shell in the DNA accent, pointer parallax. Poster: surface-2 with texture-halftone.

## Registry sections (`pnpm dss add section <id>/<variant> --page /route`)

Without a variant, a variant that fits the DNA archetype is picked with the site seed (one variant per id per site). Props mirror `example.json`.

| Section | Component | Use | Fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| contact/details | Contact | Channels as a definition list plus hours. Page-level h1 (use on the contact page). | editorial, swiss, craft, institutional, organic, luxury, architectural, minimal-mono |
| cta/band | Cta | Ink background, one line, one button. Ends a page. | editorial, swiss, brutalist, institutional, magazine, tech-noir, kinetic-type, craft |
| cta/statement | Cta | A display-size sentence that is itself the link. Quiet, confident close for refined brands. | editorial, luxury, architectural, craft, organic, minimal-mono, institutional |
| faq/accordion | Faq | Radix accordion with FAQPage structured data. | editorial, swiss, institutional, organic, playful, tech-noir, minimal-mono, craft |
| features/bento | Features | Uneven tile grid (one large tile, optional metrics), staggered reveal. Products and studios. | tech-noir, playful, kinetic-type, brutalist |
| features/numbered | Features | Ruled, numbered list beside a title column. Avoids the three-equal-cards pattern. | editorial, swiss, institutional, minimal-mono, magazine, tech-noir |
| gallery/sequence | Gallery | Scroll-snap strip of captioned photos. Needs real images. | architectural, craft, luxury, editorial, organic, magazine |
| hero/fullbleed-image | Hero | Edge-to-edge photo with an ink scrim; text bottom left. Needs one excellent real photo. | architectural, luxury, organic, craft, editorial |
| hero/kinetic | Hero | Giant looping words (CSS marquee) over a ruled statement. Agencies, music, events, bold brands. | kinetic-type, brutalist, magazine, playful |
| hero/mono-index | Hero | Monospace statement, factual lines and a numbered link index. Portfolios, consultants, studios. | minimal-mono, swiss, tech-noir, brutalist |
| hero/scene | Hero | Text left, a lazy three.js shader panel right (poster fallback). For DNA three level hero or immersive. | tech-noir, kinetic-type, playful |
| hero/split-editorial | Hero | Oversized display title left, body and actions right. Text-led, no image required. | editorial, craft, institutional, architectural, luxury, swiss |
| hero/split-media | Hero | Text and actions beside a portrait photo, optional proof facts under a rule. Needs one real photo. | institutional, editorial, craft, organic, luxury, retro-print |
| logos/marquee | Logos | Real clients or partners only. Monochrome SVG logos or names in the display face. | swiss, tech-noir, magazine, kinetic-type, playful, brutalist, institutional, editorial |
| pricing/columns | Pricing | Joined columns on hairlines, one featured plan. Products, memberships, packages. | swiss, tech-noir, playful, minimal-mono, institutional, editorial, organic |
| projects/index | Projects | Lead project with a wide image, then a ruled table. Architects, agencies, builders, portfolios. | architectural, editorial, swiss, minimal-mono, brutalist, craft |
| quote/manifesto | Manifesto | Display-size belief statement with one accent phrase. Brand pause between dense sections. | editorial, luxury, craft, architectural, kinetic-type, organic, magazine |
| services/grid-numbered | Services | Two-column numbered list on rules with price lines. Practices, consultancies, products with tiers of service. | swiss, institutional, minimal-mono, brutalist, magazine, tech-noir, playful |
| services/rows | Services | Full-width ruled rows with optional links and prices. Good for agencies, trades, clinics, restaurants (as a menu). | editorial, craft, institutional, swiss, luxury, architectural, retro-print |
| stats/figures | Stats | Display-size numbers over a rule. Proof, not decoration. | swiss, magazine, institutional, tech-noir, editorial, brutalist, kinetic-type |
| steps/timeline | Steps | Horizontal timeline with accent dots. Only for real sequences. | editorial, swiss, craft, tech-noir, playful, organic, institutional |
| story/split-media | Story | Portrait photo beside a short narrative. Needs a real photo before launch. | editorial, craft, organic, luxury, architectural, institutional |
| story/stacked | Story | Title, two text columns, then a wide captioned image. Architecture, institutions, magazines. | architectural, editorial, magazine, institutional, swiss, minimal-mono |
| team/portraits | Team | Portrait grid with roles and one-line bios. Real photos only. | editorial, craft, institutional, organic, architectural, luxury, swiss |
| testimonials/columns | Testimonials | Three equal ruled columns of quotes. Calmer than a lead quote; good for services and products. | swiss, institutional, tech-noir, playful, minimal-mono, retro-print, kinetic-type, brutalist |
| testimonials/quotes | Testimonials | One display-size quote, then a two-column list. No avatars or stars by default. | editorial, luxury, craft, institutional, magazine, organic, architectural |

## Modules (`pnpm dss module add <slug>`; read `core/modules/<slug>/README.md` after adding)

- `analytics`: Cookieless audience measurement (Plausible, Umami or Cloudflare Web Analytics), production builds only, no consent banner needed.
- `blog`: Markdown articles in content/blog: index, article pages with Article JSON-LD, RSS, sitemap and llms.txt entries.
- `forms`: Contact form: Server Action (zod, honeypot, rate limit, Turnstile) sending email through Resend.
- `legal`: Legal notice and privacy policy (GDPR, Swiss nLPD) pages linked from the footer, structured placeholders to fill.
- Database: `pnpm dss db init [--driver d1|libsql|postgres]` (schema in server/db/schema.ts, `db()` from server/db/client.ts).

## Archetypes (design.dna.ts `archetype`)

- **editorial**: a considered publication: big serif headlines, generous measure, asymmetric columns. Signature: pull quotes, drop caps, captions under images, one oversized headline per page. Avoid: card grids, icons in circles, centered everything.
- **swiss**: rational grid, flush-left grotesk, one strong signal color, numbers and alignment do the talking. Signature: visible grid, large index numbers, strict baseline, a single red/blue/yellow accent. Avoid: rounded pills, gradients, decorative serif.
- **brutalist**: raw and confident: heavy type, thick borders, system-like layout, high contrast. Signature: thick black rules, marquee text, exposed structure, offset hard shadows. Avoid: soft shadows, pastel gradients, delicate serif.
- **luxury**: restraint and space: high-contrast serif, slow reveals, a muted precious accent. Signature: huge whitespace, letter-spaced small caps, full-bleed imagery, slow fades. Avoid: bright saturated accents, dense copy, bouncy motion.
- **organic**: natural and tactile: earthy palette, soft shapes, paper texture, unhurried rhythm. Signature: organic blob crops, hand-drawn underline, warm off-white surfaces. Avoid: neon, hard black, tech grids.
- **tech-noir**: dark interface aesthetic: mono labels, fine grid lines, one luminous accent, product-first. Signature: terminal-like labels, code snippets, live-looking UI fragments, subtle 3D. Avoid: purple-to-pink gradients, glassmorphism cards, emoji.
- **playful**: cheerful and bold: rounded type, saturated colors, stickers and bouncy motion. Signature: sticker-like badges, tilted cards, color-blocked sections, springy hovers. Avoid: thin serif, grey-on-grey, corporate stock photos.
- **retro-print**: printed-matter nostalgia: slab and fat-face type, halftone, warm inks on cream. Signature: badges and stamps, two-ink color scheme, misregistered offsets. Avoid: glossy gradients, thin geometric sans.
- **minimal-mono**: almost nothing: monospace-led, monochrome, one tiny accent, content as structure. Signature: plain-text lists, timestamps, keyboard-like links, generous line height. Avoid: hero images, decorative illustration, more than one accent.
- **magazine**: newsstand energy: condensed display, dense multi-column layout, big numbers and covers. Signature: cover-style hero, issue numbers, kicker labels, tight leading headlines. Avoid: empty minimalism, pastel palettes.
- **architectural**: space and proportion: thin type, wide margins, full-bleed photography, slow motion. Signature: plan-like line drawings, image sequences, coordinates and dimensions as details. Avoid: bright accents, illustration, playful motion.
- **kinetic-type**: typography as image: oversized moving headlines, variable fonts, scroll-driven motion. Signature: viewport-wide words, variable weight on scroll, marquees, split-letter reveals. Avoid: static stock imagery, small timid headlines.
- **craft**: made by hand: documentary photos, warm serif, process stories, tactile details. Signature: process timelines with real photos, handwritten notes, maker portraits. Avoid: stock photos of smiling people, glossy UI.
- **institutional**: quiet authority: classic serif, deep sober color, clear hierarchy, proof over promises. Signature: credentials and figures up front, named people, precise service lists. Avoid: handshake stock photos, gavel icons, vague superlatives.

## Font pairings (design.dna.ts `fonts`)

- `fraunces-instrument`: Fraunces / Instrument Sans, soft optical serif, warm and contemporary (editorial, organic, craft)
- `newsreader-hanken`: Newsreader / Hanken Grotesk, news serif with a neutral grotesk (editorial, magazine, institutional)
- `instrument-serif-geist`: Instrument Serif / Geist, condensed display serif, quiet sans (editorial, architectural, luxury)
- `bodoni-figtree`: Bodoni Moda / Figtree, high-contrast didone, fashion register (luxury, magazine)
- `cormorant-manrope`: Cormorant Garamond / Manrope, airy garalde for calm, premium pages (luxury, organic, architectural)
- `gloock-onest`: Gloock / Onest, heavy contrasty serif, poster energy (retro-print, editorial, kinetic-type)
- `young-serif-public`: Young Serif / Public Sans, friendly old-style serif, honest sans (craft, retro-print, organic)
- `caslon-franklin`: Libre Caslon Display / Libre Franklin, classic American pairing, trustworthy (institutional, editorial, luxury)
- `source-serif-plex`: Source Serif 4 / IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono, serious, technical, legible (institutional, tech-noir, editorial)
- `spectral-work`: Spectral / Work Sans, screen-first serif, calm and precise (institutional, craft, architectural)
- `garamond-schibsted`: EB Garamond / Schibsted Grotesk, literary garamond, sturdy grotesk (craft, editorial, institutional)
- `space-grotesk-work`: Space Grotesk / Work Sans + Space Mono, quirky grotesk with a mono sibling (tech-noir, swiss, brutalist)
- `bricolage-familjen`: Bricolage Grotesque / Familjen Grotesk, expressive variable grotesk (playful, kinetic-type, magazine)
- `syne-manrope`: Syne / Manrope, wide, art-school display (kinetic-type, playful, architectural)
- `unbounded-onest`: Unbounded / Onest, extended rounded display, loud and modern (playful, kinetic-type, tech-noir)

- `archivo-black-chivo`: Archivo Black / Chivo + Chivo Mono, blunt heavy grotesk, industrial (brutalist, swiss, magazine)

- `familjen-public`: Familjen Grotesk / Public Sans, rational grotesk system (swiss, institutional, minimal-mono)
- `jetbrains-geist`: JetBrains Mono / Geist + JetBrains Mono, mono-led developer aesthetic (tech-noir, minimal-mono, brutalist)

- `fredoka-nunito`: Fredoka / Nunito, rounded and friendly, family or kids (playful, organic, craft)
- `italiana-tenor`: Italiana / Tenor Sans, thin fashion display, spa and boutique (luxury, architectural, organic)
- `marcellus-lora`: Marcellus / Lora, inscriptional caps with a bookish body (organic, craft, luxury)
- `alegreya-pair`: Alegreya / Alegreya Sans, calligraphic humanist superfamily (craft, organic, editorial)
- `zilla-work`: Zilla Slab / Work Sans, slab with print character (retro-print, craft, magazine)
- `bitter-public`: Bitter / Public Sans, sturdy slab, civic and dependable (institutional, retro-print, craft)
- `red-hat-pair`: Red Hat Display / Red Hat Text, open, friendly corporate superfamily (playful, swiss, tech-noir)

- `hedvig-pair`: Hedvig Letters Serif / Hedvig Letters Sans, quiet Scandinavian serif and sans (editorial, minimal-mono, organic)

## Package APIs

- `@dss/seo`: deployEnv, isIndexable, absoluteUrl, canonicalPath, rootMetadata, pageMetadata, robots, sitemap, llmsTxt, AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS, nodeId, organizationSchema, websiteSchema, localBusinessSchema, breadcrumbSchema, faqSchema, serviceSchema, articleSchema, eventSchema, buildGraph. `@dss/seo/react`: JsonLd.
- `@dss/security/server`: safeAction, formDataToObject, verifyTurnstile, memoryRateLimiter, cloudflareRateLimiter, defineEnv, clientIp.
- `@dss/site/config` (next.config.ts, manifest): defineManifest, MANIFEST_INPUT, ManifestSchema, PageSchema, OrganizationSchema, withDss, linkedCoreRoot.
- CSP presets (manifest `security.csp.presets`): turnstile, plausible, umami, cloudflareAnalytics, youtube, vimeo, calcom, googleMaps, stripe.
- `@dss/data`: id, timestamps; `/d1`: d1Db; `/libsql`: libsqlDb; `/config`: dssDrizzleConfig.
